2 MOHAMMAD NAWAZ J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -3-  NC: 2023:KHC-K:7373-DB  MFA No. 203030 of 2023  JUDGMENT
This appeal is taken up for final disposal with the consent of both the learned counsel.
2. We have heard the learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company and learned counsel appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 3/claimants.

3. The tribunal by its judgment dated 21.07.2022 passed in MVC No.5/2021 has awarded a total compensation of Rs.26,32,700/- with 6% interest p.a., for the death of one Satyanarayansingh, who died in a road traffic accident on 31.08.2019 at about 7.00 p.m. involving an Auto rickshaw bearing registration No.KA- 32/A-9017, insured with the appellant herein.

4. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that the deceased was admittedly a bachelor and therefore, the tribunal was not justified in deducting 1/3rd of his income towards personal expenses.
The same is not disputed by the learned counsel for the claimants.

The tribunal taking the income of the deceased at Rs.13,250/- and adding 40% towards future prospects and deducting 1/3rd of the said income towards personal expenses computed the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.12,366/-.
The deceased was aged 28 years and therefore, applying 17 as multiplier awarded a sum of Rs.25,22,664/- towards loss of dependency.
6. Monthly income of the deceased is rightly taken as Rs.13,250/- considering the year of accident.
The deceased being a bachelor, as rightly contended by the learned counsel for the appellant, half of his income should have been deducted towards personal expenses.
40 % of the income should be added towards future prospects.

Hence, the loss of dependency will be:
Rs.13,250/- + 40% x 1/2 x12 x 17 = Rs.18,92,100/-
7.
Under the conventional heads, wherein a total sum of Rs.1,50,000/- has been awarded by the tribunal, the claimants are entitled for another 10% which comes to NC: 2023:KHC-K:7373-DB Rs.15,000/-.
Hence, the claimants are entitled for a total compensation of Rs.20,37,100/- as against Rs.26,32,700/- awarded by the tribunal.

8. Accordingly, we proceed to pass the following:
